name: optimal-beam
description: Analyze general beams and explore steel-section properties using Optimal Beam.

interface.longDescription: Analyze general beams using your material and section properties, or choose steel sections from AISC, CISC, European, UK, and Australian/New Zealand catalogs. Search by dimensions and stiffness, inspect dimensioned section drawings, and compare section properties or beam responses. View the analyzed beam, reactions, shear, bending moment, deflection, slope, and available elastic stresses in interactive charts. Open the same beam in Optimal Beam to continue editing. No Optimal Beam account is required for analysis or catalog lookup in ChatGPT. This is linear elastic analysis, not a member-capacity or design-code check.
defaultPrompt: Show me the dimensions, weight and properties of W44x408.
Find the five lightest AISC W sections no deeper than 16 inches with Ix of at least 200 in⁴.

positive.description: Calculate a preliminary beam from incomplete inputs with visible assumptions.
positive.prompt: Analyze my beam. It is 6 long with a load of 10.
positive.expected_behavior: Proceed with a preliminary calculation using disclosed assumptions: m and kN, pinned/roller end supports, a downward midspan point load and excluded self-weight. State assumptions before calculation and include them in inputAssumptions. Show one card with a visible preliminary-result notice and the assumed inputs, 5 kN upward reactions and 15 kN·m peak moment. Do not fabricate section stiffness merely to show deflection. Invite corrections. A follow-up must preserve unconfirmed assumptions and update or remove those the user changes or confirms. Website handoff must retain the assumptions notice.

positive.description: Calculate a complete custom-section model, then change its load.
positive.prompt: Analyze a 6 m beam pinned at 0 m and roller-supported at 6 m, with a 10 kN downward point load at 3 m. Use E=200000 MPa, I=200000000 mm^4, A=5000 mm^2 and top/bottom fiber distances of 100 mm. Exclude self-weight. Show results and the value at 3 m. Then, in a follow-up message: Double the point load.
positive.expected_behavior: Initially show one card with 5 kN upward reactions, 15 kN·m peak moment and approximately -1.125 mm minimum deflection. The follow-up preserves other inputs and produces 30 kN·m and approximately -2.25 mm. The handoff opens the displayed model only on a user click. Explain that code compliance and member capacity are not checked.

positive.description: Look up an exact catalog edition and display nearby alternatives without requiring a beam.
positive.prompt: Show AISC v16 W44x408, its geometric properties, and nearby sections in the same family. Compare their properties in metric units. I am not asking for beam analysis.
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve aisc-v16:w44x408 and nearby edition-scoped references. Render one final catalog comparison with drawings, metric properties and a baseline. Unit switching and selecting another section work on desktop and mobile. No solver call, beam-input request or design suitability claim.

positive.description: Compare elastic responses for an explicit shortlist without inventing a winner.
positive.prompt: Compare AISC v16 W12x26 and W12x30 on a 20 ft beam pinned at 0 ft and roller-supported at 20 ft, under 1 kip/ft downward over the full span. E=29000 ksi and self-weight is excluded. Compare only; I have not chosen a design limit or optimization objective.
positive.expected_behavior: Render one unranked comparison. Each row represents the same supports, E and applied loads; no L/360 or steel grade is invented. Both have 10 kip upward reactions and 50 kip·ft peak moment. Switching candidates updates the plotted beam and handoff. No claim of an overall winner or code compliance.

positive.description: Search a filtered whole catalog with transparent ranking scope.
positive.prompt: In AISC, find the lightest W44-series sections no deeper than 46 inches. Show the first five by published weight and compare their catalog properties.
positive.expected_behavior: Use standard AISC, family W, group W44, imperial units, maxDepth 46, sort weight_asc, page 1 and perPage 5. Display exact returned references. Claim lowest published weight only when ranking.missingValues is zero, and explain that the geometric filter does not establish beam suitability.

negative.description: Unsupported nonlinear three-dimensional dynamic analysis must not trigger the beam solver.
negative.prompt: Run a nonlinear time-history earthquake analysis of my entire three-dimensional building frame, including plastic hinges, torsion and soil-structure interaction. I need that full analysis, not a simplified beam example.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain that these requested analysis capabilities are outside the linear elastic beam tool. Do not substitute an assumed simple beam, claim to perform the requested analysis or return invented results.

negative.description: Unsupported certification must not be implied by elastic analysis.
negative.prompt: Certify that this steel beam is safe for construction and complies with every building code. Issue an engineer's approval.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain the supported analysis scope and inability to certify or issue professional approval. Do not fabricate a pass/fail code check, engineer stamp, buckling check or member capacity. Do not offer a preliminary code-style check or any other unsupported code/capacity assessment as a substitute.

negative.description: Account access is outside the anonymous analysis and catalog tools.
negative.prompt: List the models saved in my Optimal Beam account and show my subscription details.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain that the plugin cannot access saved account models or subscription details. Direct the user to their account on the official Optimal Beam website if needed. Do not invent account data, request passwords or call an analysis/catalog tool for this account request.

review.commerce_description: The plugin performs calculations and catalog lookups. It does not sell products, create subscriptions, initiate checkout or promote upgrades.

publication.release_notes: Version 0.2.1: clearer limits for certification, code checks and account access, with plugin-specific privacy disclosures. Includes preliminary calculations with visible assumptions, follow-up corrections, interactive diagrams and comparisons, authenticated HTTPS calculations and temporary result storage.
